stages.title: Marketing Fundamentals: Audience, Value & Funnel
stages.description: How to define who you are marketing to, why they should choose you, and how a prospect moves from awareness to loyal customer.
learningObjectives: Define a buyer persona and describe how one is built from research
Write a value proposition that is clear, compelling and differentiating
Name the main funnel stages (awareness, consideration, conversion, loyalty/retention) and a tactic for each
Explain why the real customer journey is less linear than the funnel model suggests

explainBack.question: You are launching a new product. How would you describe your target customer, state why they should buy from you, and map the steps they take from first hearing of you to buying again?
rubric: A buyer persona is a research-based profile representing a segment of the target audience, covering goals, motivations and pain points, not just demographics
Personas are built from quantitative data (analytics, CRM) plus qualitative research such as customer interviews
A good value proposition is clear (names the offering and benefit), compelling (motivates action) and differentiating (sets it apart from competitors)
Funnel stages: awareness (discover the brand/problem), consideration (compare options), conversion (purchase), loyalty/retention (repurchase and recommend)
Real journeys loop between exploration and evaluation, so the funnel is a simplification; satisfied customers can feed new awareness

resources.title: How To Create a Buyer Persona (FREE Template)
resources.description: HubSpot's short walkthrough of what a buyer persona is and how to fill in a persona template for your business.
keyPoints: Promises a definition of a buyer persona
Walks through a free persona template
Shows what research questions feed a persona

resources.title: How to Create Detailed Buyer Personas for Your Business
resources.description: Defines buyer personas as research-based profiles of audience segments and lays out a five-step process from data gathering to validating them.
keyPoints: Persona = research-based profile of a target-audience segment
Goes beyond demographics to goals, motivations and pain points
Combine analytics/CRM data with interviews and focus groups
Most businesses need a handful of personas; review them at least yearly
Negative personas describe poor-fit prospects to avoid

resources.title: What Is a Value Proposition?
resources.description: Open-textbook section defining a value proposition and the three qualities that make one effective.
keyPoints: A value proposition summarises why a customer should buy
Must be clear: names the offering and its benefit quickly
Must be compelling: motivates the buyer to act
Must be differentiating: sets the offer apart from alternatives
Answers who it is for, what it is, and why it is uniquely valuable

resources.title: Marketing funnel
resources.description: Glossary entry explaining the marketing funnel's stages, typical tactics at each, and how the modern journey departs from a straight line.
keyPoints: Awareness (TOFU): discovery via social, search and ads
Consideration (MOFU): comparison via email nurturing, webinars, case studies
Conversion (BOFU): purchase via trials, demos, testimonials
Loyalty: repurchase and referral
Journeys loop; some use a circular 'flywheel' model

stages.title: Content Marketing & Editorial Planning
stages.description: How to plan useful content around a few themes, pick formats, schedule it on an editorial calendar and reuse it across channels.
learningObjectives: Define content marketing and how it differs from direct promotion
Choose content pillars and match content formats to goals
Build an editorial calendar with the core fields and a publishing cadence
Repurpose one piece of content into several formats

explainBack.question: Explain what content marketing is and describe how you would plan a quarter of content for a small brand, including themes, formats, scheduling and reuse.
rubric: Content marketing creates and distributes valuable, relevant, consistent content to attract and retain a clearly defined audience, rather than directly pitching products
Content pillars are a few recurring themes (e.g. educate, entertain, inspire, promote), each tied to a goal such as awareness or leads
Formats include blog posts, video, podcasts, infographics, social posts and interactive content, chosen for the audience and channel
An editorial calendar records topic, content type, channel, due/publish dates, owner and status
Repurposing turns one asset (e.g. a research report) into blog posts, short videos, newsletters and other pieces

resources.title: Content Marketing Strategy in 7 Minutes
resources.description: A seven-minute overview from Semrush of how to put together a content marketing strategy.
keyPoints: Promises a fast overview of content strategy
Covers setting goals and knowing the audience
Touches on planning and distributing content

resources.title: What Is Content Marketing?
resources.description: The Content Marketing Institute's standard definition of content marketing and why organisations use it.
keyPoints: Defines content marketing as valuable, relevant, consistent content for a defined audience
Aims to attract and retain, not hard-sell
Benefits cited: sales, cost savings, loyalty
Says strategy should be documented

resources.title: How to leverage content marketing, according to a content marketer
resources.description: Guide covering content formats, a nine-step strategy process, editorial calendars, content remixing and pillar/cluster structure.
keyPoints: Lists formats: blog, video, podcast, infographic, social, interactive
Nine steps from audience and SMART goals to analysis
Recommends a publishing schedule for consistency
Remix one research report into articles, videos, newsletters
Pillar page plus linked supporting articles

resources.title: Social media content creation: 15 pro tips, tools + templates [2026]
resources.description: Practical content-creation tips including choosing content pillars and giving each a goal.
keyPoints: Pick a handful of content pillars and set a goal for each
Common pillars: educate, entertain, inspire, promote
Promotional posts usually pair with a call to action
Batching content saves production time

resources.title: How to Create an Editorial Calendar in 7 Easy Steps
resources.description: Defines an editorial calendar and gives seven steps to build one, with the fields to track for blogs, social and other formats.
keyPoints: Editorial calendar = plan of what, where, when and who
Set cadence based on budget and resources
Core fields: topic, content type, due/publish date, owner, status
Audit existing content to find pieces to repurpose

stages.title: Social Media Marketing
stages.description: How to choose platforms for your audience, combine organic and paid social, and measure engagement correctly.
learningObjectives: Distinguish organic from paid social and the job each does
Choose platforms using audience data rather than guesswork
Calculate engagement rate and know what counts as engagement
Outline the steps of a social media strategy, including SMART goals and consistent posting

explainBack.question: A local brand asks whether it should just post more or pay for ads on social media. Explain organic versus paid social, how you would pick platforms, and how you would measure engagement.
rubric: Organic social is free content posted to build community and trust; paid social (boosted posts, ads) buys reach with precise targeting
Organic reach is limited by platform algorithms, so a common approach is to test content organically and put ad budget behind top performers
Platform choice should follow audience data, e.g. Pew finds YouTube and Facebook most used by US adults and younger adults far more likely to use Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat
Engagement rate by reach = total engagements on a post / reach of that post x 100; impressions and views alone are not engagement
A strategy starts with SMART goals and audience research, and is refined with analytics

resources.title: Paid vs. Organic Social: A Complete Guide
resources.description: Animoto's explainer contrasting paid and organic social media and how they work together.
keyPoints: Promises definitions of paid and organic social
Compares strengths of each
Discusses combining both

resources.title: Organic vs paid social media: Everything you need to know
resources.description: Explains organic and paid social, the organic reach problem, and a hybrid approach that uses organic results to steer ad spend.
keyPoints: Organic = free posts that build relationships
Paid = boosted posts and ads with precise targeting
Algorithms show organic posts to only part of your followers
Boost organic winners with paid budget

resources.title: Social Media Fact Sheet
resources.description: Nonpartisan survey data on what share of US adults use each social platform, broken down by age and education.
keyPoints: YouTube (84%) and Facebook (71%) most used by US adults in 2025
Instagram 50%, TikTok 37%
Younger adults use Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat much more
LinkedIn use rises with education level

resources.title: Master your 2026 social media strategy [free template + expert tips]
resources.description: A seven-step social strategy guide from SMART goals and audience research to measuring and refining.
keyPoints: Set SMART goals first
Research audience down to platform
Audit and benchmark against competitors
Post consistently with a clear voice
Use analytics to decide where paid budget goes

resources.title: How to calculate engagement rate: 2026 formulas & benchmarks
resources.description: Six engagement-rate formulas (by reach, post, impressions, daily, views, cost) with what counts as engagement and benchmarks.
keyPoints: ER by reach = engagements / reach x 100
ER by impressions suits paid campaigns
Likes, comments, shares, saves count as engagement
Impressions and views alone are exposure, not engagement

stages.title: Email Marketing: Consent, Segmentation & Deliverability
stages.description: How to build an email list lawfully, segment it, read open and click rates, and meet mailbox providers' authentication rules.
learningObjectives: State the core legal rules for marketing email under CAN-SPAM (US) and PECR/UK GDPR (UK)
Segment a list by demographic, behavioural and engagement criteria
Define open rate and click rate and know their tracking limits
Explain SPF, DKIM and DMARC and Gmail's sender requirements

explainBack.question: You are starting a newsletter for an online shop with US and UK customers. How will you collect addresses lawfully, segment the list, measure performance and make sure the emails reach inboxes?
rubric: CAN-SPAM requires accurate headers, non-deceptive subject lines, a valid postal address and a clear opt-out honoured within 10 business days; it does not itself require prior consent
In the UK (PECR) marketing email to individuals needs specific consent, except the 'soft opt-in' for existing customers buying similar products with an opt-out offered each time
Segmentation divides subscribers by criteria such as location, demographics, purchase behaviour or engagement so content is more relevant
Open rate and click rate are percentages of successfully delivered emails; opens can be inflated by bots/Apple Mail Privacy Protection
Gmail requires all senders to use SPF or DKIM and keep spam rates below 0.3%; senders of 5,000+ messages/day need SPF, DKIM and DMARC plus one-click unsubscribe

resources.title: CertMike Explains DMARC, DKIM and SPF
resources.description: A short explainer by IT educator Mike Chapple on how SPF, DKIM and DMARC authenticate email.
keyPoints: Promises what SPF does
Explains DKIM signing
Explains how DMARC builds on both

resources.title: CAN-SPAM Act: A Compliance Guide for Business
resources.description: The FTC's official guide to the US commercial email law: its main requirements, opt-out timing and penalties.
keyPoints: No false headers or deceptive subject lines
Identify ads and include a valid postal address
Clear opt-out; honour it within 10 business days
Penalties up to $53,088 per violating email

resources.title: Electronic mail marketing
resources.description: ICO guidance on when UK organisations may send marketing emails and texts to individuals, including the soft opt-in.
keyPoints: Need specific consent to email individuals
Soft opt-in only for existing customers and similar products
Soft opt-in does not cover bought lists
Every message needs an easy opt-out

resources.title: How Email Segmentation Drives Engagement and ROI
resources.description: Defines email segmentation and lists common ways to divide subscribers, with the engagement benefits.
keyPoints: Segmentation = dividing subscribers into groups by criteria
Criteria: demographics, location, behaviour, engagement, funnel stage
Relevant content lifts opens and clicks
Better engagement helps sender reputation

resources.title: About Email Reports
resources.description: Help article defining open rate, click rate and bounces in campaign reports and how bot activity distorts them.
keyPoints: Open rate = % of delivered emails registering an open
Click rate = % of delivered emails registering a click
Opens need images loaded or a tracked click
Bots and Apple MPP can inflate opens

resources.title: Email sender guidelines
resources.description: Google's requirements for anyone sending to Gmail accounts, with extra rules for bulk senders.
keyPoints: All senders: SPF or DKIM, TLS, valid DNS
Keep spam rate under 0.3% (aim for under 0.1%)
5,000+/day: SPF and DKIM plus DMARC (policy can be none)
Bulk marketing mail must support one-click unsubscribe

stages.title: Paid Advertising (PPC) Basics
stages.description: How pay-per-click auctions work, what CPC/CPM/CPA mean, how ad quality affects cost and position, and how to target audiences.
learningObjectives: Explain CPC, CPM and CPA bidding and match each to a goal
Describe how Google's ad auction ranks ads (Ad Rank) and what you actually pay
Explain Quality Score's components and that it is a diagnostic, not an auction input
Choose audience segments (affinity, in-market, custom, your data) for targeting
Calculate click-through rate

explainBack.question: Explain to a new advertiser how a Google search ad auction decides which ads show and what they pay, which bidding option to pick for their goal, and how to read Quality Score and CTR.
rubric: CPC = pay per click (traffic); CPM/vCPM = pay per 1,000 (viewable) impressions (awareness); CPA = target a cost per conversion and needs conversion tracking
Ad Rank uses bid, ad and landing page quality, Ad Rank thresholds, auction competitiveness, search context and asset impact; actual CPC is often below the max bid
Quality Score (1-10) reflects expected CTR, ad relevance and landing page experience and is a diagnostic tool, not an input to the auction
Audience segments include affinity (interests), in-market (actively researching), custom (keywords/URLs) and your data (past visitors/customers), usable for targeting or observation
CTR = clicks / impressions (e.g. 5 clicks from 100 impressions = 5%)

resources.title: Quality Score EXPLAINED: The TRUTH About Ad Rank and Ad Quality [Inside Google Ads Episode 107]
resources.provider: Jyll Saskin Gales | Google Ads Coach
resources.description: A Google Ads coach (and former Googler) explains how Quality Score relates to Ad Rank and ad quality.
keyPoints: Promises to separate Quality Score from Ad Rank
Explains what ad quality means in the auction
Clears up common Quality Score myths

resources.title: Understanding bidding basics
resources.description: Google's overview of bidding by clicks, impressions, conversions and video views, and which goal each suits.
keyPoints: CPC: pay when someone clicks
vCPM: pay per 1,000 viewable impressions
CPA: set what you will pay per conversion
Conversion bidding needs conversion tracking
Match bidding to the business goal

resources.title: About Ad Rank
resources.description: Explains how Ad Rank decides ad eligibility and position and why you often pay less than your maximum bid.
keyPoints: Ad Rank decides eligibility and position
Factors: bid, quality, thresholds, competition, context, assets
Actual cost is often below max bid
Higher quality can mean lower CPC

resources.title: About Quality Score for Search campaigns
resources.description: Defines Quality Score, its 1-10 scale and three components, and states it is not used in the auction.
keyPoints: Keyword-level score from 1 to 10
Components: expected CTR, ad relevance, landing page experience
Diagnostic tool, not an auction input
Components rated above/average/below vs. last 90 days

resources.title: About audience segments
resources.description: Describes Google Ads audience segment types and how they can be used for targeting or observation.
keyPoints: Affinity: interests and habits
In-market: actively researching purchases
Custom: defined by keywords, URLs, apps
Your data: people who interacted with you (remarketing)
Segments can target or just observe

resources.title: Clickthrough rate (CTR): Definition
resources.description: Defines click-through rate and gives the formula with a worked example.
keyPoints: CTR = clicks / impressions
5 clicks from 100 impressions = 5%
High CTR suggests ads are relevant
Used to spot weak keywords and ads

stages.title: Analytics & Measurement
stages.description: How to tag campaigns, track events and key events in GA4, understand attribution, and compute ROAS and CAC.
learningObjectives: Build campaign URLs with UTM parameters
Explain GA4 event types and mark key events (conversions)
Compare data-driven and last-click attribution in GA4
Calculate ROAS and customer acquisition cost (CAC)

explainBack.question: You are running an email and paid-social campaign. Explain how you would tag the links, record sign-ups as conversions in GA4, credit channels for sales, and judge whether the spend was worth it.
rubric: Tag links with utm_source, utm_medium and utm_campaign (always use these three); utm_term and utm_content are optional extras
GA4 events are automatically collected, enhanced measurement, recommended or custom; important actions are marked as key events
Attribution assigns credit to touchpoints; GA4 offers data-driven and last-click models, and first click, linear, time decay and position-based were removed in November 2023
ROAS = conversion value / ad spend x 100% (e.g. $5 sales per $1 spend = 500%)
CAC = (sales + marketing costs) / number of new customers; it is often compared with customer lifetime value (CLV)

resources.title: GA4 Key Events – How to Track Conversions in Google Analytics 4 (2025 Update)
resources.description: Loves Data, a Google Analytics training channel, shows how key events are used to track conversions in GA4.
keyPoints: Promises what key events are
Shows marking an event as a key event
Explains how conversions now appear in GA4

resources.title: [GA4] URL builders: Collect campaign data with custom URLs
resources.description: Lists the UTM parameters GA4 reads, which three to always include, and an example tagged URL.
keyPoints: Always use utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign
utm_term for paid keywords; utm_content for creative variants
Example: ?utm_source=summer-mailer&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=summer-sale
Campaign URL Builder tool available

resources.title: [GA4] About events
resources.description: Explains GA4's four event categories, how events are processed, and marking important events as key events.
keyPoints: Automatically collected, enhanced measurement, recommended, custom
Custom events need custom reports
Mark important actions as key events
Verify with Realtime and DebugView

resources.title: [GA4] Get started with attribution
resources.description: Defines attribution and the models available in GA4, noting which older models were retired.
keyPoints: Attribution assigns credit along the path to a key event
Data-driven uses ML on converting and non-converting paths
Paid and organic last click gives 100% to last click
First click, linear, time decay, position-based removed Nov 2023

resources.title: About Target ROAS bidding
resources.description: Describes Target ROAS bidding and gives the ROAS formula with a worked example.
keyPoints: ROAS = conversion value / ad spend x 100%
$5 sales per $1 spend = 500% ROAS
Target ROAS bids to hit a return goal

resources.title: Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC): Definition, Formula, and Key Metrics
resources.description: Defines customer acquisition cost, its formula and included costs, and the CLV:CAC ratio.
keyPoints: CAC = (sales + marketing cost) / new customers
$400,000 / 500 customers = $800 CAC
Includes ad spend, salaries, creative, tools
Common target CLV:CAC around 3:1

stages.title: Conversion Rate Optimization & A/B Testing
stages.description: How to design focused landing pages and run valid A/B tests that improve conversion rate.
learningObjectives: Calculate conversion rate
Describe what makes a landing page focused on one call to action
Run an A/B test: hypothesis, single change, random split, analysis
Explain statistical significance and why tests need enough traffic

explainBack.question: Your landing page converts at 2%. Describe how you would test a new version properly and decide whether it really won.
rubric: Conversion rate = conversions / interactions (e.g. 50 / 1,000 = 5%)
A landing page is a standalone campaign page with a single goal (call to action) and fewer links than a homepage
An A/B test randomly splits traffic between a control (A) and a variant (B), starting from a data-based hypothesis and changing one element at a time
Statistical significance is the likelihood the difference is not due to chance; a 95% confidence (p = 0.05) threshold is typical
Tests need enough traffic/sample size and should run at least one business cycle; A/B tests show what changed, not why

resources.title: Don't A/B Test Yourself Off a Cliff
resources.description: Nielsen Norman Group's short video on the risks of relying only on A/B testing to make design decisions.
keyPoints: Promises pitfalls of over-relying on A/B tests
Argues tests need a sound hypothesis
Pairs testing with understanding users

resources.title: Conversion rate: Definition
resources.description: Defines conversion rate and gives the formula with an example.
keyPoints: Conversion rate = conversions / interactions
Can exceed 100% when counting every conversion

resources.title: What Is a Landing Page?
resources.description: Explains what a landing page is, how it differs from a homepage, its main types and core elements.
keyPoints: Standalone page built for a campaign
Single focus: one call to action
Fewer links than a homepage
Types: lead generation and click-through
Elements: headline, CTA, short form, social proof

resources.title: What is A/B testing?
resources.description: Glossary entry defining A/B testing and laying out a six-step testing process.
keyPoints: Randomly split traffic between control A and variant B
Start from data and a hypothesis
Make targeted, measurable changes
Analyse results for statistical significance

resources.title: Statistical significance
resources.description: Explains statistical significance, p-values, confidence intervals and why tests fail to reach significance.
keyPoints: Significance = likelihood the difference is not chance
Larger samples give more reliable results
Low baseline rates make significance harder
Run at least one business cycle

resources.title: A/B Testing 101
resources.author: Tim Neusesser
resources.description: NN/g's introduction to A/B testing: requirements, the 95% significance norm, and limitations.
keyPoints: Tests variations with a live audience against set metrics
Needs high traffic
Change one element at a time
Typical threshold 95% (p = 0.05)
Shows what happened, not why

stages.title: Strategy, ROI, Privacy & Advertising Ethics
stages.description: How to judge marketing return and the privacy and disclosure rules (GDPR, India's DPDP Act, FTC, ASCI) that shape digital campaigns.
learningObjectives: Calculate ROI and distinguish it from revenue
State what valid consent means under UK GDPR
Summarise the consent and penalty basics of India's DPDP Act and Rules
Apply FTC and ASCI rules on disclosing paid endorsements and influencer posts

explainBack.question: You are planning an influencer and data-driven campaign in India and the UK/US. How will you judge whether it pays off, what consent rules apply to customer data, and how must influencers disclose the partnership?
rubric: ROI = (revenue - cost of goods sold) / cost of goods sold; it measures profit relative to cost, not just revenue
Under UK GDPR, consent must be freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous via a clear affirmative act; pre-ticked boxes or silence do not count and withdrawal must be easy
India's DPDP Rules 2025 require a separate, clear consent notice from each Data Fiduciary, let people withdraw consent, and allow penalties up to Rs 250 crore
The FTC requires influencers to disclose any financial, employment, personal or family relationship clearly in the post itself (e.g. 'ad', 'sponsored'), not hidden in bios or hashtag piles
ASCI requires upfront, prominent labels such as 'Ad', 'Sponsored', 'Collaboration' or 'Partnership' for any material connection; advertisers and influencers share responsibility

resources.title: EP 118. Disclosures 101: FTC Guidelines for Social Media Influencers
resources.description: A law podcast episode walking through the FTC's 'Disclosures 101' guidance for influencers.
keyPoints: Promises a walkthrough of FTC influencer guidance
Covers when a disclosure is required
Covers how to make disclosures clear

resources.title: About return on investment (ROI)
resources.description: Explains ROI for advertising with the formula and a worked example.
keyPoints: ROI = (revenue - cost of goods sold) / cost of goods sold
ROI shows profitability, not just sales
Helps decide where to spend budget

resources.title: What is valid consent?
resources.description: ICO guidance on the elements of valid consent under UK GDPR.
keyPoints: Consent: freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous
Requires a clear affirmative act
Pre-ticked boxes and inactivity are not consent
Must be easy to withdraw; keep records

resources.title: DPDP Rules, 2025 Notified
resources.provider: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
resources.description: Government release summarising India's DPDP Rules 2025: consent notices, rights, roles and penalties.
keyPoints: Rules notified November 2025 with 18-month phase-in
Separate, clear consent notice required
Consent can be withdrawn at any time
Penalties up to Rs 250 crore

resources.title: Disclosures 101 for Social Media Influencers
resources.description: FTC guidance on when and how influencers must disclose brand relationships.
keyPoints: Disclose financial, employment, personal or family ties
Put disclosure in the post, not just bio or hashtags
Use clear words like 'ad' or 'sponsored'
In video, disclose in the video itself

resources.title: ASCI Social Media Disclosure Guidelines
resources.description: ASCI's rules for influencer disclosure in India, including approved labels and placement.
keyPoints: Any material connection needs disclosure
Labels: Ad, Sponsored, Collaboration, Partnership, Free gift, etc.
Must be upfront and prominent
Virtual influencers must disclose they are not human
